title: Documenting Units in Prose Instead of Types
pattern: Comments detailing the physical units (meters, milliseconds, bytes) of primitive parameters.
why_bad: No compiler enforcement. Prose cannot prevent developers from passing feet instead of meters or seconds instead of milliseconds. Strong type patterns resolve this error at compile time.
detection: Comments on parameters containing terms like 'in meters', 'in ms', 'in milliseconds', or units describing primitive types.
counterexample: FFI or serialization boundaries where primitives are mandatory; there, unit-suffixed names (`latency_ms`) plus doc-comments are the practical limit.
fix: Refactor primitives to custom types or wrapper structs representing the units (e.g., `std::time::Duration`), removing the units comment.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 32 ("Are units on data declarations commented?"); John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 13.2.
